alignments.note: Expletive *there* rides with the expressed copula under rule 9.
The negator carries the clause's whole negation *nothing*; the complement is a plain adjective and no negative indefinite stands in the Greek, so rules 41 and 59 do not empty it.
ἐὰν μή rendered by the single *save*; the English answers to neither particle separately, rule 39.
Purpose conjunction realized by the word introducing the English clause, rule 40.
Supplied subject and passive auxiliaries ride with the subjunctive; head on the lexical verb under rules 9 and 17.

The Greek leaves the subject unexpressed and the ASV supplies *anything*, which rides with this inflected verb under rule 9, discontinuously around it under rule 15; head on the lexical verb word. Rule 68 is the competing reading and does not reach this clause: it is scoped in its own terms to a verbless clause whose copula the ASV supplies, whereas ἐγένετο is expressed, and the chapter puts every other supplied subject on its finite verb (4:1, 4:12, 4:24, 4:37).
Predicate adjective left bare on *secret*, the supplied subject belonging to the expressed verb.
Second purpose conjunction rendered *that*, as at s007; rule 24.
Supplied subject and modal ride with the subjunctive; head on the lexical verb.

review_notes: Corrected: the supplied subject *anything* (t014) moves from ἀπόκρυφον to ἐγένετο. Rule 68 opens by scoping itself to a verbless clause's supplied copula and subject, and this clause expresses its verb, so rule 9 governs and the predicate keeps only its own word.
The negation *nothing* stays whole on οὐ: no negative indefinite token stands in the Greek for rules 41 and 59 to hand it to.
